news.title: Free school meals for every family on Universal Credit
news.summary: Since September 2026, every child in England whose family gets Universal Credit can have free school meals. Ask your school if your children are signed up.
news.why: You get Universal Credit and have school-age children.

news.title: New energy price cap is announced in late November
news.summary: Ofgem sets the most energy firms can charge from January to March. We'll update your 60 days when it's out.
news.why: You pay for energy by direct debit, so your payment could change in January.

news.title: Warm Home Discount: £150 off your electricity bill
news.summary: If you get Universal Credit, you should get £150 off this winter without applying. If it hasn't arrived by March, contact your energy supplier.

news.title: Bank of England updates its view on prices
news.summary: The Bank of England's latest report says how fast it expects prices to rise next year. Food and energy prices matter most for your budget.
news.why: Most of your spending goes on food, energy and bills.

news.title: Help with food and bills in Manchester
news.summary: Manchester City Council has one page that lists help with food, energy and emergency costs, and how to ask for it.

news.title: Hours went down? Your Universal Credit can go up
news.summary: Universal Credit looks at what you earned each month. In a month with fewer shifts, your payment the next month should be higher.
news.why: You work zero-hours and get Universal Credit.

news.title: Plan Christmas spending before December
news.summary: MoneyHelper has a free planner. Write down who you're buying for and a limit for each, then stick to the total.
news.why: Your tightest weeks are around Christmas.

news.title: Check you're getting every benefit you can
news.summary: Free, private benefit calculators take about 10 minutes. Many families miss help they can get.
news.why: Your pay changes every week, so what you can get may change too.
